messages:
olivia (Design): dropped a quick prototype: https://figma.redwood.example/file/sparkline-interaction

olivia (Design): proposal: add tiny inline annotations on the p95 sparkline where latency regresses concurrently with throughput spikes. goal: help teams correlate RPS->latency without clicking into details. annotations = small triangular markers on the line.

tere (Eng UI): small markers sound useful. caution: p95 stroke is thin at small sizes. we might need a 1.5px hit area for keyboard/focus but keep visual mark minimal. Also need to avoid clutter when many events are close.

olivia (Design): agreed. sketch shows collapse behavior: overlapping markers merge into a stacked badge with a tooltip listing events. default color: #e24b4b for latency-coupled spikes, #ff9f43 for throughput-only spikes. legend copy: "Annotations: latency+throughput / throughput-only".

chen (PM): product question: what's the detection logic? we should be explicit in tooltip copy. users will ask why something was flagged.

olivia (Design): detection: event types come from observability stream: "rps_spike", "latency_regression". annotation rule: place combined marker when both occur in same time bucket (configurable window). tooltip shows cause breakdown and sample confidence.

dex (SRE): backend can emit combined flags. note on sampling: if heatmap uses reservoir sampling we still compute regressions on full telemetry and surface confidence. we'll add a "confidence" score 0-100.

contrast-bot: a11y check: ensure marker has at least 3:1 contrast against the chart background; markers should expose an accessible name and be reachable via keyboard.

tere (Eng UI): keyboard interactions: tab cycles marker -> Enter/space opens small inline flyout anchored to the sparkline with details + actions (open traces, zoom). Flyout should be dismissible with ESC. We'll implement as an accessible button with aria-expanded.

olivia (Design): copy for flyout header: "Event details". lines: "Time: 12:03:22", "Peak p95: 320ms (+120ms)", "Peak RPS: 1.4k", "Confidence: 82%". Actions: [Zoom to 5m] [Open traces] [Open logs].

chen (PM): copy tweak: replace "Zoom to 5m" with "Zoom to spike window" to avoid implying a fixed duration. Keep labels short. Also add a one-line explanation in tooltip: "Annotations highlight correlated traffic and latency changes."

tere (Eng UI): visual note: ensure z-index keeps flyout over everything and markers behind focus ring when focused. Also add reduced-motion preference respect (no pulsing animations).

dex (SRE): perf note: if we render many small flyouts on hover that could be heavy. prefer single flyout instance reused for whichever marker is focused/hovered, populated dynamically.

olivia (Design): acceptance criteria for design -> 1) markers collapse when dense, 2) accessible button for each marker with aria-label e.g., "Annotation: latency + traffic at 12:03, confidence 82%", 3) flyout content matches product fields, 4) respects reduced-motion & a11y color/hatch modes, 5) legend toggle persists.

contrast-bot: a11y reminder: in high-contrast mode swap to patterned marker (diagonal hatch) and ensure focus outline >=3px. Also provide text alternative in the flyout for screen readers summarizing the event.

tere (Eng UI): implementation plan: canvas for sparkline, svg overlay for markers to keep interaction easy. will prototype keyboard + screenreader behaviors.

chen (PM): one more product thought: add a small "why this matters" tooltip for each annotation type in the legend guiding users on triage steps.

olivia (Design): will add microcopy: "Latency+Traffic: look for overloaded downstreams or queuing. Throughput-only: check ingress throttles or bursts."

tere (Eng UI): i'll spin up a dev build with the svg overlay and basic flyout. aim for an experiment behind a feature flag to 5% of users.

dex (SRE): we'll expose the event feed and confidence metric from backend RFC. I'll coordinate on sampling docs.

olivia (Design): thanks team  i'll upload updated frames and finalize microcopy. ping when the dev build is up. :sparkles:

chen (PM): thanks all!
